A live, hand-written physics engine — running right now

Drop it. Fling it. Watch it tumble.

Tumble Lab is a 2D physics playground built from scratch in vanilla JavaScript — no engines, no frameworks, just a Verlet integrator solving thousands of constraints a second. Everything above is simulated live. Click the canvas to drop more.

Open the sandbox → Browse scenes

tip: click the canvas to drop balls

What's inside the box

A real solver, not a video

Every body you see is integrated frame-by-frame from first principles. Position-based Verlet keeps ropes and cloth jiggling believably; an iterative relaxation pass holds structures together; a spatial hash makes hundreds of collisions cheap.

Bouncing bodies

Spawn elastic balls with momentum, gravity, restitution and air drag. They pile, stir, and settle like real beads.

Ropes & chains

Distance constraints chained together swing, sag and whip under load. Pin them, hang them, or let them fly.

Tearable cloth

A constraint grid that folds, ripples, and snaps thread-by-thread when you overstretch it. Grab it and rip a hole.

Stacking crates

Soft-rigid boxes braced by diagonal constraints. Build a tower, then fling a ball through it and watch it topple.

Gravity wells

Switch to attract/repel mode and drag a field around the canvas. Slingshot bodies, herd them, or scatter them.

Particle flourish

Fireworks, confetti and velocity-coloured motion trails — all optional, and automatically toned down for reduced-motion.

Eight ready-made scenes

Pick a sandbox and start playing

Ball Pit, Rope Bridge, Cloth Flag, Tearable Cloth, Box Stack, Zero-G Drift, Fireworks and Newton's Cradle — each one launches straight into the live sandbox with the right gravity, bounce and friction dialled in.
